anomalies.observed: The ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch is drawn as T5, an AO3400A (30 V, ~5.7 A SOT-23 N-channel MOSFET): ATO_VALVE drives its gate through R10 (100 Ω) and it is pre-driven by T4 (BT3904). No AON6407 (T3) appears at the valve; the only other power MOSFET in the drawing is the series device in the +24 V input path (reverse-polarity protection, with R7 33k and D3 12 V).
anomalies.expected: The specification lists the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch as T3, an AON6407 8-DFN N-MOSFET, whose gate is driven through R10 (100 Ω) and pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).

evidence.quote: T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).
ATO solenoid valve (via T3/T4 switch, ATO_VALVE net)
ATO Valve driver block: ATO_VALVE → R10 100Ω → T5 (AO3400A); FLOAT_HIGH → R11 4k7 → T4 (BT3904), R12 10k

anomalies.impact: The valve is switched by a much smaller device than the intended AON6407. If the 24 V solenoid's steady/inrush current approaches the AO3400A rating the switch can overheat or fail, and the populated part no longer matches the specified BOM.

parsed.summary: The drawing agrees with the specification almost everywhere (buck/LDO power train, ADM3260 pH/EC isolation, TMC2209 drivers with 110 mΩ sense resistors, 2.2 kΩ I2C pull-ups, float-switch pull resistors), but the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch is built with T5 (AO3400A) whereas the spec calls for T3 (AON6407), so the valve driver is populated with a different, much smaller MOSFET than intended.
